attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his essay, citing his own earlier newsletter.

semantics.note: The normalised version drops 'in part', so it reads as if the two causes are the whole explanation. It also leaves out the clause that costs are subsidized and unprofitable for model providers. The contract's 'materially contribute' test puts the partial causation back.

contract.note: Reading 'losing money' as attributable net losses in Q2 2025, and costs as total delivery spending, is an ordinary plain reading. The speaker gave no period, population, or accounting basis, so how these are read does shape the result.

evidence.note: Measures API prices at fixed capability, not providers' total delivery costs or profits. Does not refute rising total spending.
Replit's own account of longer agent runs raising its costs. One company, no loss figures, no industry-wide breakdown.
Midjourney said it was profitable in 2022, outside the target quarter, with no measure given. Cannot serve as a Q2 2025 counterexample.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no comparable accounts showing losses across providers in Q2 2025, and no breakdown of what caused them. The only profitability counterexample is from 2022. The price-trend data measures a different metric. Nothing in the packet settles the universal loss claim or the causal mechanism.

attribution.note: Zitron presents the figure as confirmed by his source, so it is his own endorsed assertion.

semantics.note: Keeps the August 2025 date, 'around', active licensed users, the 1.81% figure, and the 440M denominator.

contract.note: Matching on product, month, the 28-day activity window, and licence status is a fair, ordinary reading. It sensibly rules out non-independent repetitions of the same claim.

evidence.note: Microsoft disclosure: 100M+ monthly users across all Copilot apps, consumer and commercial. Wrong scope for the M365 Copilot licensed count.
Microsoft disclosure: 15M paid seats in January 2026. Later date and a different metric (paid seats, not August active users).

reviews.rationale: No independent August 2025 count of active licensed users and no matching subscriber denominator was found. Microsoft's disclosures cover different scopes and dates, so they neither confirm nor contradict the figure.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his essay.

semantics.note: Keeps the universal 'every user' claim and the stated cause (consistent cost control is impossible).

contract.note: The plain reading (user-level revenue minus serving cost, paying users included) follows the surrounding text and is fair. The unstated accounting basis and cost allocation affect the result.

evidence.note: Anthropic's spend limits for API customers (Sept 2024) are a customer-side control. They show nothing about provider serving costs or per-user profitability.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no user-level revenue and serving-cost records to confirm the universal loss claim or supply a verified counterexample. Customer spend limits do not show whether providers can consistently control their own costs. Unresolved.

semantics.note: A fair condensation. 'These users' means the August 2025 active licensed population, a scope the contract restores.

contract.note: Requiring evidence that some users actually paid below $30, not just that a discount was offered, is a strict but ordinary reading of 'aren't all paying'.

evidence.note: A reseller dated 11 July 2025 advertised a 15% Copilot discount running Jul–Sep 2025. Shows the discount was available, not that anyone took it up.

reviews.rationale: The only readable evidence is an advertised promotion covering August 2025. That makes below-list prices plausible but does not document a discounted purchase. The reporting on actual discounts could not be read. Under the contract, this is unresolved.
